about.title: Exeter Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Exeter is a small city, but its main corridors — Kaweah Street, Palm Avenue, Visalia Road, and Firebaugh — carry a steady flow of local and pass-through traffic, and crashes still happen even here, most often on Monday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. when commuters and school traffic overlap. Whether you were stopped at a light, turning off Visalia Road, or rear-ended near downtown, the aftermath can be confusing: medical bills arrive, an insurance adjuster calls, and you're left wondering what your next step should be. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured people in Exeter with independent personal injury attorneys who understand how Tulare County claims work. There's no cost to get connected, and the attorneys in our network only get paid if you recover compensation. You don't have to figure this out on your own or navigate calls from the other driver's insurer without support.
commonInjuries: Cuts, bruises, and soft tissue damage

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: California's Filing Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity (like the city or county) is involved. Waiting too long can cost you the chance to recover anything at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce What You Recover
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces your payout. An attorney can help make sure the insurer doesn't unfairly shift blame onto you.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: The other driver's insurance company may ask for a recorded statement early on — before you know the full extent of your injuries. It's generally safer to let an attorney handle those conversations so nothing you say gets twisted later.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim after a crash in Exeter?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If your crash involved a government vehicle or a hazard on a city or county road, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Kaweah Street and Palm Avenue see a lot of local traffic — does that affect my claim?
items.answer: The volume of traffic on a road doesn't change the legal standards that apply to your claim, but it can affect how evidence is gathered, like witness accounts or nearby camera footage. An attorney can help make sure that evidence is preserved before it disappears.

items.question: Should I give a statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and doing so before speaking with an attorney can work against you. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that minimize payouts, so it's usually best to let a legal representative handle that communication.
